title: Maine’s data center revolt will decide who controls the Senate
slides: Maine voters just drew a line in the sand
A town rejected a data center. Why does it matter?
It could tip control of the U.S. Senate
Your electricity bill may become a ballot issue
Ask candidates: data centers or residents first?
thread_text:
1. A town just said no

Maine voters rejected a data center project at the ballot box. It's the first time residents directly blocked one—and it could reshape how AI infrastructure gets built nationwide.

2. Why one town matters

This isn't just local noise. The vote could tip control of the U.S. Senate, because the data center fight is now a political litmus test in a swing state.

3. Your bill is next

Electricity costs are becoming a ballot issue. As data centers suck up power, utilities are passing the tab to residents—and voters are noticing.

4. The question for candidates

Politicians are now being asked: data centers or residents first? The answer may decide who wins in November.

5. Ask them directly

At the next town hall or debate, ask your candidate: 'Do you side with data centers or residents on power costs?' Their answer tells you everything.

instagram.caption:
A town in Maine just voted down a data center at the ballot box — the first time residents have directly blocked one. 🗳️

This wasn't a zoning board decision. It was a public vote, and it's turning data centers into a campaign issue in a swing state.

That fight could decide who controls the U.S. Senate. ⚡

Meanwhile, as data centers pull more power, utilities are shifting the cost to household bills — and voters are starting to connect the dots.

If you write about energy, AI, or politics, this is the story that ties all three together. 💡

Next town hall, ask your candidate: data centers or residents first? Their answer tells you everything.
